dimensions.evidence: Expression 1/((1-f)+f/s) combines dimensionless fraction f with dimensionless factor s; output S dimensionless (unit 1). All three variables declared dimensionless. No unit conversion needed or applied; pure literal 1 only.

guards-inverses.evidence: Guards f in [0,1], s>0; rejection cases cover f=1.5 (domain) and missing s. Inverse algebra independently verified: from 1/S=(1-f)+f/s, f=(1-1/S)/(1-1/s); substitution S=1.2,s=2 gives (1/6)/(1/2)=1/3, matching the Berkeley case; s=f/((1/S)-(1-f)) follows from the same rearrangement. Boundaries documented: f=0 gives S=1 (checked), f=1 gives S=s, s->inf gives 1/(1-f); s=1 leaves f underdetermined and s<=0 is excluded by guard rather than offered as a solve direction. Final sentence correctly denies causal invertibility.

reference-independence.evidence: All three references independently recomputed: 1/(0.7+0.15)=1/0.85=1.17647 rounds to the published 1.18 within tolerance 0.005; 1/(2/3+(1/3)/2)=1.2 exactly as published; f=0 gives 1 as a definitional boundary. The two published oracles were verified on the inspected pages (Wikipedia p=0.3/s=2 result; Berkeley third-by-2 result), so provenance claims of 'published result from inspected source' hold; the third is labeled a boundary identity, not a measurement.
